6bf3c638d3aa2c44fbd458ed1854c4690271371a.summary: Insikt Group of Recorded Future reports an ongoing campaign since May 2022 by the group OilAlpha, which it says likely supports a pro-Houthi movement agenda. Targets reportedly include non-governmental, media, humanitarian and development entities interested in Yemen, including people attending Saudi Arabian government-led negotiations. The group reportedly uses spoofed Android apps, encrypted messengers and link shorteners, and the report names the SpyNote, SpyMax and njRAT remote access tools. hedges: The report says linking the group to threat actors that likely support a pro-Houthi movement agenda is an assessment.
The group is described as highly likely to have targeted non-governmental, media, humanitarian and development entities.
Targeting of persons at Saudi Arabian negotiations and spoofed apps are described as reportedly occurring.
As of writing, the report suspects the attackers targeted individuals the Houthis wanted direct access to.
Victimology assessment suggests most targets were Arabic-language speakers using Android devices.
Espionage involvement is described as highly likely; njRAT samples suggest other malware may have been used for testing or attacks.
Expected continuation depends on the absence of new information or broader geostrategic shifts.
